finding: Per-molecule strained prevalence 0.4429 -> 0.5143 (z=+0.85) and the per-RING closure-policy shape 0.1679 -> 0.1948 (z=+0.77): neither improved, both edged up. Meanwhile molecules shrank 28.70 -> 26.87 heavy atoms, rings per molecule fell 3.74 -> 3.30, and ring-forming events per trajectory fell 3.31 -> 2.86. Quality rose 0.171 -> 0.300 (z=+1.79). The ring-size histogram moved the wrong way chemically: 6-membered rings 152 -> 111 while 3-membered rings 26 -> 38. So the quality gain is consistent with producing smaller, less ring-dense molecules rather than with better ring chemistry. Holding molecule size fixed, ring strain has NO detectable effect on QED at EITHER checkpoint (+0.033+-0.039 and -0.037+-0.037) while size does (-0.024 per heavy atom, |z|~8); the SA strain penalty is real at both (+0.791+-0.217 and +0.496+-0.218).

validity_over_attempts.note: denominator is ATTEMPTS. valid_state_fraction over COMMITTED endpoints is 1.0 in both arms (the architectural guarantee).

question: Does continued training from step 1000 to step 2500 remove the de-novo small-ring defect?
verdict: NO. The defect does not improve; the closure-policy shape is flat-to-worse. The modest quality gain is attributable to smaller, less ring-dense molecules.
